item.text: {"chapter_id":"8B","issues":[{"issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0024-E007","BATCH-0016-E001","BATCH-0048-E014"],"explanation":"The draft lacks a sufficiently explicit frozen program portfolio. These candidates identify major goals beyond security: austerity, poverty reduction, energy and food self-sufficiency, infrastructure, labor policy, international and climate commitments, and the stated pacification strategy. Without them, the selected evidence risks judging only security, pensions, and flagship projects.","recommended_action":"add"},{"issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0052-E001","BATCH-0052-E002","BATCH-0052-E004","BATCH-0052-E006"],"explanation":"The draft uses one budget item but omits the stronger 2023 monitoring evidence: differing program universes, unclear target populations, nearly 20% of priority-program budgets in programs without clear problem definitions or results measurement, disregarded recommendations, and deterioration in selected program logic. These are decisive for priorities, implementation, and adaptation.","recommended_action":"add"},{"issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E003","BATCH-0032-E010","BATCH-0051-E001","BATCH-0051-E004"],"explanation":"Health-system execution is absent despite being a major governing priority and a central adverse outcome. The candidates document the Seguro Popular/INSABI/IMSS-Bienestar transition, worsened access, operational challenges, formal 2023 rules, and prescribed audit and correction mechanisms. The draft's health-access summary is too narrow without the implementation chain.","recommended_action":"add"},{"issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0026-E020","BATCH-0018-E015"],"explanation":"The draft omits appointments and institutional staffing capacity. Vacancies and impaired or later court-forced appointments at INAI, COFECE, and IFT directly bear on 8B.4, 8B.5, and 8B.8, especially whether the ruler selected, retained, or failed to empower capable implementers.","recommended_action":"add"},{"issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E007","BATCH-0016-E008","BATCH-0016-E009","BATCH-0016-E011"],"explanation":"The draft includes the National Guard performance proxy but omits the surrounding decisive series: security spending reallocation, staffing and certification, mixed crime trends, measurement caveats, and subnational comparative analysis finding that greater Guard activity was not consistently associated with homicide reduction. The existing entry is therefore under-contextualized and cannot support a complete security execution summary.","recommended_action":"add"},{"issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0012-E015","BATCH-0013-E016","BATCH-0026-E017","BATCH-0048-E006"],"explanation":"Plan B and the resulting mass mobilization and Supreme Court invalidation are omitted. This is a major 2023 test of formal program execution, institutional resistance, crisis management, and adaptation. It also supplies contrary evidence to a simple narrative of administrative failure by showing functioning opposition and judicial correction.","recommended_action":"add"},{"issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E010","BATCH-0029-E003","BATCH-0031-E003"],"explanation":"The draft mentions no crisis-response evidence for Hurricane Otis, despite the guide's explicit crisis-management lens. Candidates provide presidential access and decision evidence, troop and aid deployment, reported delays and distribution failures, and an independent account of the response. This is a decisive omitted 2023 crisis case.","recommended_action":"add"},{"issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0040-E008","BATCH-0030-E004"],"explanation":"The Maya Train entry should be supplemented with the external-audit evidence of unsubstantiated right-of-way expenditures, advances lacking completed ownership documents, and incomplete transfer to the Sedena-controlled company. The current summary mentions cost and incomplete construction but omits the strongest audit-based evidence on administrative control, financial execution, and unresolved accountability.","recommended_action":"add"},{"issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0013-E006"],"explanation":"The draft includes pension delivery but omits the end-period medicine-warehouse intervention, its stated 24–48-hour delivery mechanism, and the prior prescription-shortage baseline. This is an important contrasting case of late implementation and an untested corrective response.","recommended_action":"add"},{"issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0042-E008","BATCH-0051-E024","BATCH-0052-E007"],"explanation":"The draft lacks independent program-design and procurement-quality evidence. These candidates show direct-allocation and publication risks, weak results orientation, poor linkage between components and objectives, and mixed target compliance. They would materially test whether budgets and formal plans became disciplined implementation.","recommended_action":"add"},{"issue_type":"irrelevant_selection","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0044-E010"],"explanation":"The decree establishes a formal security program but the draft gives it no substantive policy content or implementation result. As currently summarized it is largely a formal-architecture item and adds little beyond the stronger court and National Guard evidence.","recommended_action":"reconsider"},{"issue_type":"duplication","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E008","BATCH-0032-E006"],"explanation":"The selected National Guard performance and pension items are both useful, but the draft already concentrates on these two themes while omitting health, electoral institutions, appointments, crisis response, and fiscal/procurement controls. The imbalance makes the reading list repetitive in substantive coverage even without literal duplicate IDs.","recommended_action":"reconsider"},{"issue_type":"period_problem","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E006","BATCH-0031-E016"],"explanation":"The pension and poverty/health summaries rely mainly on 2022 outcomes entering 2023, not observed full-year 2023 outcomes. The summaries correctly add caveats, but the reading list should label these as lagged baseline evidence and add direct 2023 monitoring or end-period evidence.","recommended_action":"correct"},{"issue_type":"attribution_problem","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0016-E008"],"explanation":"The summaries appropriately note that agency noncompliance and performance proxies do not prove personal presidential direction, but they still present them as central adverse evidence without pairing them with evidence of presidential authority, orders, follow-up, or failed correction. Add candidates such as BATCH-0013-E001, BATCH-0013-E003, or BATCH-0049-E005 to preserve the attribution chain.","recommended_action":"add"},{"issue_type":"unsupported_summary","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0030-E004","BATCH-0032-E006","BATCH-0031-E016"],"explanation":"The overview says 'major security and project failures' and 'mixed social outcomes,' but does not identify the full governing portfolio, the favorable macroeconomic or labor results, or the distinction between formal delivery, attributable outcomes, and inherited or external causes. Passage review is needed to ensure the overview does not imply broader causal conclusions than the selected passages support.","recommended_action":"correct"},{"issue_type":"material_omission","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0052-E010","BATCH-0052-E015","BATCH-0052-E020"],"explanation":"The draft omits contrary and mixed implementation evidence from UN and World Bank reviews: coordinated labor, care, refugee, and violence-prevention initiatives; only eight of 24 partnership objectives achieved; project cancellations, restructurings, turnover, and changing priorities. These are needed to avoid a dossier dominated by rights, security, and flagship-project failures.","recommended_action":"add"},{"issue_type":"balance_problem","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0052-E014","BATCH-0051-E013","BATCH-0051-E016","BATCH-0031-E008"],"explanation":"The selected list is materially adverse-heavy and underrepresents positive or mixed evidence on 2023 growth, minimum-wage implementation, macroeconomic restraint, USMCA success, fiscal management, and social-program reach. These facts do not erase failures, but they are necessary for an ideology-neutral, portfolio-wide effectiveness assessment.","recommended_action":"add"}],"missing_perspectives":["Explicit 2018 program baseline across policy, state-building, regime-control, social, energy, and international goals.","Health-system transition and medicine-delivery implementation.","Appointments, personnel quality, vacancies, and institutional empowerment.","Electoral Plan B, opposition mobilization, judicial resistance, and executive adaptation.","Hurricane Otis and other direct 2023 crisis-management evidence.","Independent procurement, audit, program-monitoring, and correction records.","Positive or mixed macroeconomic, labor, social-program, UN, and World Bank implementation evidence.","End-period durability evidence beyond one incomplete infrastructure project."],"overall_assessment":"The draft is relevant but materially incomplete and too concentrated on security militarization, Ayotzinapa, the older-adult pension, poverty/health outcomes, and the Maya Train. It omits decisive evidence for the frozen program, personnel, health implementation, electoral conflict, crisis response, audits, adaptation, and contrary achievements. Several summaries are careful about attribution and lag, but the overview still risks overgeneralizing from a narrow and adverse-heavy sample. Passage review is required for the broad claims about the ruler's overall effectiveness and durability."}
